newsitem.title: USA: Osmonics sees Q2 net exceeding estimates.
newsitem.headline: Osmonics sees Q2 net exceeding estimates.

text.p: Osmonics Inc chairman and chief executive Dean Spatz said he expects the company's second quarter 1997 earnings to exceed the mean analysts' estimate of $0.20 per share.

"We think that estimate of $0.20 is a little bit on the low side," Spatz told Reuters following Osmonics' shareholder meeting here Wednesday. "But if we don't sell any investments, it may not be a whole lot higher than that."
First Call's mean estimate is for $0.20 a share in the quarter, compared to $0.21 in the second quarter of 1996.
Spatz estimated second quarter sales would be $43 million, a 19 percent increase over the year ago quarter for the maker of fluid purification membranes and equipment.
"In the first quarter of 1996, we saw a lot of orders from beverage companies, so second quarter sales last year were down, compared to the first quarter," Spatz said.
Without comparable sales in this year's first quarter, second quarter sales will show a strong quarter-toquarter improvement, he said.
"If you compare $43 million (in second quarter sales) with $36 million (in second quarter 1996 sales), that's a big increase," he said.

Osmonics said it is striving to achieve a second quarter gross margin which improves upon the 38.6 percent it registered in the first quarter and begins to approach the 41.5 percent it had in the second quarter of 1996.
Spatz also said Osmonics would shave its selling, general and administrative costs to 22 percent of sales in 1997.
At $35.1 million, SG&A costs were 22.5 percent of Osmonics $155.9 million in sales in 1996.
